stories.headline: Google DeepMind adds native audio and steering to Genie 4 world simulation
stories.summary: Google DeepMind says Genie 4 generates interactive worlds with native audio, dialogue and real-time steering while using Gemini models to improve coherence. The research preview targets trusted testers and possible training environments for robots and agents. Google also documents limits in object permanence, spatial consistency, readable text and sustained long-session behavior.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn which engineering checks matter before using generated worlds: measure interaction latency, continuity, object permanence, audio alignment and long-session drift, then separate an impressive research preview from a dependable simulation environment.

stories.headline: Salesforce links continuous agent evaluation to quarantine and cost limits
stories.summary: Salesforce announced Agent Evals, API Evals and spending controls for Agent Fabric, its cross-platform control plane. The company says tests can run before deployment and against production thresholds, trigger approval-based quarantine or a kill switch, and stop requests at budget limits. Product availability and performance claims remain vendor-reported rather than independently benchmarked.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn a production control pattern that connects quality tests, API-change checks and spending thresholds to named interventions. Use it to design ownership, approval, quarantine and recovery steps before a live agent drifts or overspends.

stories.headline: Anthropic reports early Claude-assisted results across six drug-development partners
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.summary: Anthropic describes work with six drug-development organizations across molecule design, laboratory iteration and operational research. Partner cases include a shorter CAR-T genetic design, thousands of antibody candidates and automated lab loops. The results are early, largely preclinical and partner-reported, so they demonstrate workflow possibilities rather than validated medicines or general scientific reliability.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn where AI can assist multidisciplinary research without replacing evidence: translate goals into designs, connect proposals to laboratory tests, preserve iteration records and keep scientific reviewers responsible for interpreting early findings and deciding what advances.

stories.headline: Salesforce survey finds isolated AI work creates duplication and handoff delays
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.summary: A Salesforce survey of 250 U.S. executives reports that privately used AI tools often leave outputs unshared, duplicate colleagues’ work and stall handoffs. Respondents also described time lost switching among tools. The small, vendor-sponsored sample measures executive perceptions rather than observed productivity, but it offers concrete questions for workflow audits and collaboration design.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn to audit AI work as a team process: record where prompts, evidence and outputs live, identify duplicated effort, define handoff owners and measure switching time before purchasing another isolated assistant or declaring productivity gains.

stories.headline: Oracle puts approved business workflows behind a ChatGPT workspace
stories.summary: Oracle says AI Workspace will connect ChatGPT with Fusion Applications, NetSuite, its database, cloud services and approved enterprise data. Employees can describe business goals, retrieve information and complete authorized workflows while existing governance, permissions and approvals remain in force. The announcement describes planned product capabilities; customer outcomes and broad availability are not independently established.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn how to frame a noncoding agent request around a business goal, permitted records and approval boundaries. Before action, review the selected systems, evidence, permissions and exception route, then keep the accountable owner in control.

audience_fit.practical_action: Describe one business goal, permitted records and acceptable action in ordinary language before the workspace assembles the proposed workflow.
audience_fit.review_action: Check every selected system, cited record, permission, approval point and exception route before authorizing the proposed action.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A bounded, evidence-backed business workflow that a named manager can approve, reject or return for correction.

stories.headline: IBM turns agent identity and short-lived access into a reusable review procedure
stories.summary: IBM announced Agent Identity and expanded Vault controls for AI agents, including ownership records, least-privilege permissions, short-lived credentials and real-time revocation. Watsonx Orchestrate is also positioned to discover and evaluate agents across several platforms. These are vendor product claims, but they support a reusable access-review procedure before any business agent receives authority.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn one reusable Agent Skill: record the agent owner, task, allowed systems, credential lifetime, approval rule and revocation trigger; have a human reviewer approve that access card before activation and retain its audit evidence.

stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable Agent access-review Skill: capture the named owner and bounded task; list only required systems and data; set least-privilege permissions and credential lifetime; require a human approval; define denial and real-time revocation triggers; save the decision and resulting audit evidence for the next review.
stories.related_coverage: Converts identity and credential controls into a repeatable noncoding approval checklist for business owners.

audience_fit.review_action: Have the accountable human compare requested access with the task, remove unnecessary permissions and approve or reject activation.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable reviewed access decision with bounded authority, a revocation plan and preserved audit evidence for later reassessment.

videos.focus: Turning early agent deployments into bounded operating lessons for business teams
videos.summary: Salesforce presents Box and Engine leaders discussing practical lessons from early agent deployments. The companion story emphasizes that organizational change is difficult even when teams find efficiency and customer-experience opportunities. The evidence is publisher-hosted customer discussion, so readers should treat benefits as reported experience rather than independent comparative proof.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the discussion to separate a promising agent use case from the operating changes required to support it. Ask who owns the workflow, which customer outcome is measured and what evidence would justify broader deployment.

videos.title: Todd’s Take: Securing identity in the age of AI
videos.focus: Applying human identity discipline to agent and non-human access
videos.summary: Okta CEO Todd McKinnon explains why agents create identity risk when they use service accounts, machine identities and sensitive resources across systems. The companion article covers visibility, access control, threat monitoring and Cross App Access. The lesson reflects Okta’s product perspective, so its architecture claims require independent evaluation in each environment.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the lesson to inventory every identity an agent can assume, the resources each identity reaches and the evidence retained for review. That turns an abstract agent-security concern into a bounded access-control and lifecycle exercise.

Limit each identity to required resources and record who can revoke or rotate its access when the workflow changes.
Retain action, grant and review evidence so investigators can reconstruct which identity performed each automated operation.

It is a practitioner interview, not a controlled comparison of AI security tools.
